# How the conference pages fit together

Everything for the conference lives in the `conferences/` folder of the
website project:

```
conferences/
  index.qmd                  the main conference page
  index.css                  conference styles
  images/                    logo, hotel photo, and other images
  data/                      local copies of the Google Sheet content
  _update-conference.R       script that pulls the Sheet into data/
  cfp/index.qmd              call for proposals
  preconference/
    index.qmd                workshops listing and pricing
    workshop_1/index.qmd     one folder per workshop (script-built)
  archive/                   past conference years
  _template/                 master copy for starting a new year
```

## The main page is the hub

`conferences/index.qmd` is what visitors see when they choose your
conference from the site's Conferences menu. Near the top it has a grid of
icon tiles linking to each section and to the two sub-pages. The sections
on the page are: General Information, Submissions, Hotel Information,
Schedule, Registration, and Preconference Workshops.

## The Google Sheet and the data folder

Facts that change during the year (announcement notes, deadlines, booking
and registration links, rates, and the workshop list) live in the AP-LS
Conference Google Sheet. Running `conferences/_update-conference.R` copies
them into `conferences/data/` and builds the workshop pages. The pages
read those local files when they render, so the published site never
depends on Google being reachable.

## The sub-pages

Two topics get their own pages so they can grow through the year without
crowding the main page:

- `cfp/index.qmd` holds the call for proposals.
- `preconference/index.qmd` lists the workshops and their prices. The
  listing grid builds itself from the workshop folders, which the update
  script creates from the Sheet.

## Archive and template

`archive/` holds one folder per past year, including that year's `data/`
folder, so archived pages stay frozen in time. When your conference ends,
your pages move there and the next year starts from
`conferences/_template/`. The underscore in the name keeps the template
out of the published site.

## Things you rarely touch

- `index.css` controls the look of the conference pages. Change it only if
  the web editor asks you to.
- The R code chunks in the pages move Sheet values onto the page. They are
  machinery; edit the Sheet instead.
